requirements.subject: Invalid authenticator rejection
preconditions: An account identifier and an authenticator are submitted to the trusted authentication boundary.
outcomes: Invalid or incorrect authenticators do not establish an authenticated session.
Protected operations remain denied until trusted verification succeeds.
forbiddenBehaviors: Issuing an authenticated session after failed authenticator verification.
Returning an account-existence signal through equivalent unauthenticated failure responses.
requirements.rationale: ZD-AUTH-004 requires trusted verification but does not explicitly state the incorrect-authenticator negative outcome as an acceptance criterion.

basis.description: The negative authentication outcome must be directly testable, rather than inferred from the positive verification path.
NIST SP 800-63B-4 and OWASP Authentication Cheat Sheet provide authentication-verification and failure-handling guidance.

acceptanceCriteria.given: An account identifier is submitted with an invalid or incorrect authenticator.
acceptanceCriteria.when: The trusted service evaluates the authentication attempt.
acceptanceCriteria.then: No authenticated session is issued and protected operations remain denied.

acceptanceCriteria.given: Equivalent unauthenticated attempts use an invalid authenticator with an existing identifier and an unknown identifier.
acceptanceCriteria.when: The service returns the authentication result.
acceptanceCriteria.then: The externally observable response does not reveal whether the account exists.

requirements.subject: Atomic trust state during credential replacement and session revocation
preconditions: A credential replacement or recovery event requires revocation of one or more existing sessions.
outcomes: The service never exposes an inconsistent state that leaves a credential or session required to be revoked authoritative.
Interrupted transitions are safely recoverable and do not re-authorize revoked credentials.
forbiddenBehaviors: Leaving a compromised credential/session authorized because only part of a multi-record state change persisted.
Re-authorizing a credential marked as superseded or revoked.
requirements.rationale: ZD-AUTH-020 and ZD-AUTH-021 specify recovery and revocation outcomes but do not explicitly cover partial writes or interruption between the related durable state changes.

basis.description: The product-level trust outcome must remain safe across interrupted state transitions without prescribing a database or transaction implementation.
OWASP Session Management and Forgot Password guidance supports invalidating affected sessions after credential recovery.

acceptanceCriteria.given: A credential replacement requires session revocation.
acceptanceCriteria.when: The state transition is interrupted at any persistence boundary.
acceptanceCriteria.then: The system does not expose a state in which a credential or session required to be revoked remains authorized.

acceptanceCriteria.given: A credential replacement/session-revocation transition is retried after interruption.
acceptanceCriteria.when: The trusted service evaluates the account and its sessions.
acceptanceCriteria.then: The result is a consistent completed or safely recoverable state and no revoked credential is re-authorized.

requirements.subject: Renewable session credential rotation
conditions: This requirement applies only if the selected session design supports renewal using a refresh or renewal credential.
preconditions: A renewable session credential has been issued under an owner-approved session policy.
outcomes: Successful renewal follows a documented credential-rotation policy.
Detected reuse does not silently create additional valid sessions.
forbiddenBehaviors: Allowing a superseded renewal credential to renew a session.
Creating multiple valid sessions from unrecognized replay of the same renewal credential.
requirements.rationale: ZD-AUTH-010 covers rotation at authentication and security-sensitive boundaries but does not explicitly cover renewal-credential rotation and replay if session renewal is selected.

basis.description: Renewal replay behaviour must be explicit if a renewable session mechanism is chosen; no renewal mechanism is assumed.
OWASP Session Management Cheat Sheet discusses session renewal and rotation.

acceptanceCriteria.given: A renewable session is active and a valid renewal credential is presented.
acceptanceCriteria.then: The service issues the next credential under the documented policy and rejects the superseded renewal credential.

acceptanceCriteria.given: A renewal credential is replayed or reused concurrently.
acceptanceCriteria.then: It does not silently create additional valid sessions and applies the documented revocation/recovery response.
